extracted.intended_audience: researchers of peer review and rebuttal dynamics; conference program chairs; authors seeking guidance on effective rebuttals; NLP/ML researchers studying review systems
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical analysis of which review/rebuttal features and author strategies are associated with reviewer score changes (increase, decrease, keep) in conference peer review, using ICLR 2024–2025 data and LLM-based categorization. Includes taxonomy design, predictive modeling, and practical guidance for authors and chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall rating score (before the rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer's initial overall numeric rating prior to the rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as one of the most important predictive features of subsequent score change; largely outside authors' control but strongly correlates with whether scores increase, decrease, or stay the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mean overall rating score of other reviewers (before the rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average of other reviewers' initial overall ratings for the same paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong predictor of a given reviewer's subsequent score change (peer influence); authors have limited control over this but it substantially affects rebuttal outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer engagement (number of notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: How much a reviewer participates in the discussion (e.g., number of notes or messages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High engagement can lead to either increases or decreases in scores; authors can respond to engagement but the effect depends on the reviewer's willingness to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution score (before the rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric subscore capturing perceived contribution/novelty before rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among pre-rebuttal features that predict score changes; limited direct control for authors at rebuttal time but relevant for modeling outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness score (before the rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric subscore reflecting perceived methodological soundness prior to rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An important baseline predictor for score dynamics; many rebuttals do not change soundness judgments even when overall score changes occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidence score (before the rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer's self-reported confidence in their evaluation prior to rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a model feature; interacts with other features to predict score-change likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-backed clarification (strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rebuttal strategy that provides concrete evidence, clarifications, or data to address reviewer concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual analysis highlights this strategy as strongly associated with positive score changes—use precise, evidence-supported responses rather than vague claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic/vague defense (strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal responses that are nonspecific, vague, or provide generic defenses without concrete evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tends to only help reviewers maintain their original scores (i.e., little positive impact); authors should avoid relying on generic or vague defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evasive stance (strategy/stance subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses that avoid directly addressing reviewer points or that deflect criticisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associated with maintaining original scores rather than improving them; evasive replies are unlikely to persuade reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bare agreement/disagreement (strategy subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simply stating agreement or disagreement with reviewer points without further elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When combined with evidence or clarification, bare agreement/disagreement can help increase scores; unelaborated positions alone are weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disagree (stance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly disagreeing with reviewer claims (may be accompanied by justification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can influence scores depending on justification quality—simple disagreement without evidence is less persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method details (strategy subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing additional methodological specifics or clarifying algorithmic/experimental details in the rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often useful to resolve misunderstandings; adding clear method details can improve reviewers' assessments if it addresses their concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future promise (strategy subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promising future work, extensions, or improvements as part of the rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tends to be a weaker persuasive strategy than present, evidence-backed fixes; relying mainly on future work is unlikely to yield positive score changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad assertion (strategy subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Making wide-ranging claims or broad statements without supporting evidence or specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associated with poorer outcomes; reviewers respond better to precise, evidence-based replies than to sweeping assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal precision and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which rebuttal text is precise, directly addresses reviewer concerns, and clearly explains fixes or clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual analysis indicates precise responses are strongly associated with positive score changes; authors should aim for concise, targeted, and well-supported replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of vague or defensive tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal tone that is defensive, evasive, or vague rather than explanatory and evidence-based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vague or defensive rebuttals have little effect on scores; adopt a factual, clarifying tone and avoid emotional or evasive language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting borderline papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness that rebuttals primarily affect borderline submissions (papers near acceptance thresholds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically, rebuttals most often influence borderline papers (approx. 20% of accepted submissions likely benefited from rebuttal-driven score increases); authors of borderline papers should invest effort into strong rebuttals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer disagreement dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: How reviewer score disagreement changes after rebuttal (e.g., disagreements narrow for high-scoring submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebuttals tend to reduce disagreement among reviewers for high-scoring papers, but low-scoring papers remain largely unaffected; authors should consider this when prioritizing rebuttal content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weakness categories (taxonomy)—unclear writing
rubrics_metrics.description: One common weakness reviewers flag: unclear or poorly written exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve clarity and presentation in rebuttal and revisions; unclear writing is a frequent driver of low scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weakness categories (taxonomy)—weak baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that experimental comparisons use weak or inappropriate baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address by adding stronger comparisons, clarifying baseline choices, or providing additional experiments if feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weakness categories (taxonomy)—limited datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Concern that datasets are too small/limited to support claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should clarify dataset limitations, justify choices, or provide additional analyses demonstrating robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weakness categories (taxonomy)—poor/unclear algorithmic description
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer notes that algorithmic or technical descriptions are incomplete or confusing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide targeted method details and clarifications in rebuttal to reduce misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength categories (taxonomy)—novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive reviewer assessment that the paper introduces novel ideas or contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight novelty succinctly in rebuttal and clarify how contributions differ from prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength categories (taxonomy)—methodological soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise that the methods and experiments are sound and well-justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforce soundness by clarifying experimental design and addressing potential methodological concerns directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength categories (taxonomy)—efficient model or approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of efficiency or practical advantages of the proposed approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete evidence (e.g., runtimes, parameter counts) when responding to efficiency-related questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength categories (taxonomy)—clear presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive assessments of well-organized, clear exposition and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clarity in rebuttals and use them to remove any residual points of confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation framing: classification of score-change outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Modeling score changes as a three-class problem (Increase, Decrease, Keep) and alternatively as a two-class problem (Increase vs Decrease/Keep).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of labeling affects class balance and performance (three-class macro F1=0.52, two-class macro F1=0.71 in this study); interpret results with awareness of class imbalances and modeling limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics and class-imbalance considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of macro F1 and per-class F1 to evaluate predictive models, with attention to class sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macro F1 correlates with class sizes; report per-class scores and consider merging minority classes if warranted. Perform multiple runs and report mean(std).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducible modeling/procedures (data splits, normalization, hyperparameter search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental procedures: data split (training 80%, validation 10%, test 10%), feature normalization fit on training data, grid search over class weights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow reproducible procedures (document splits, normalization, model seeds, prompt versions); authors reported prompts, code, and derived data under CC BY 4.0 for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-assisted annotation reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Using LLMs (GPT-4o) with prompts to label review strengths/weaknesses and rebuttal strategies, with iterative prompt refinement and expert validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLM judgments are imperfect; refine categories and prompts with human experts and measure agreement (the chosen prompt achieved 84% pairwise human agreement in validation). Treat LLM labels as helpful but noisy signals.
